content:
## Source
.design/m5/48-tpm-signing.md — REQ-3, AC-2, AC-7 + decomposition PR 3.

## Surface
- `polaris-backend/src/labeler/signer/tpm/seal.rs` — sealing logic
- `polaris-backend/src/labeler/signer/tpm/pcr.rs` — PCR policy construction (default PCR0/4/7)
- Extends `TpmSigningKey::new()` to consult the policy on load and fail with `SealPolicyMismatch` on PCR drift.

## Rust-quality notes
- **PCR set is operator-configurable** via `[labeler.signing_key.tpm] pcrs = [0, 4, 7]` config — defaults if absent.
- **`PcrSet` newtype** wrapping `Vec<u32>` with validation (non-empty, all in `[0, 23]` range, sorted, deduplicated). Per rust-quality §2 — newtype for the validated form.
- **`Esys_PolicyPCR` session creation**: at startup, construct a sealing policy via the configured PCR set + their current TPM-reported digests. Validate against the seal-time policy before load.
- **AC-7 (exfiltration test)**: cross-machine VM-snapshot test verifies unseal fails with `SealPolicyMismatch` on a host with different PCR values. This is the security property of the entire epic.
- Per rust-quality §5 + §7: any `unsafe` block (there should be none in this file) gets `// SAFETY:` + a miri exercise.

## External references
- TPM 2.0 PCR usage: https://uapi-group.org/specifications/specs/linux_tpm_pcr_registry/
- tss-esapi PolicyPCR: https://docs.rs/tss-esapi/latest/tss_esapi/

## Acceptance (AC-2, AC-7)
- [ ] AC-2: PCR-mismatch fixture test — change a PCR value between seal and unseal → `TpmError::SealPolicyMismatch`. Process memory contains NO private key bytes after the failed unseal (verified by `procfs` memory inspection in test harness).
- [ ] AC-7: VM-snapshot exfiltration test — snapshot a sealed deployment, restore on a different host, unseal fails.

- Blocks #158 (init command uses sealing).
